cards.text: Last time, about three thousand of Israel's men went up against the city of Ai, and they fled (Joshua 7:4). The sin that cost them has been dealt with (Joshua 7:12, 26). Now the LORD speaks to Joshua, Israel's leader: "Do not be afraid or discouraged."

cards.question: This time, how much of the army does the LORD tell Joshua to take up to Ai?

cards.text: Then the LORD says, "See, I have delivered into your hand the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land." HAVE delivered. The battle hasn't even STARTED, friend. When I say a batch is done, I'm guessing. When God says it, it's DONE.

cards.question: The LORD says to do to Ai what was done to Jericho, except this time Israel may keep the plunder and livestock for themselves.
The LORD also gives Joshua a plan for taking Ai. What is it?

answers.text: Set up an ambush behind the city
March around the city seven times
Wait for the city to surrender

cards.text: So Joshua and the whole army set out to attack Ai. Joshua picks 30,000 mighty men of valor and sends them out at night.
His orders: lie in ambush behind the city, not too far from it, and all of you be ready. Then Joshua and the rest will march on Ai, and Ai will come out against them like the first time.

cards.question: When the men of Ai come out, what will Joshua and his troops do?

cards.text: Joshua says Ai will chase them until they're drawn away from the city. Running away ON PURPOSE, friend, which is more than I can say for the time a fly chased me across the bakery.

cards.question: Why does Joshua expect the men of Ai to fall for Israel's retreat?

answers.text: They'll think Israel is running like before
They'll think Israel is out of supplies
They'll think Joshua has been hurt

cards.question: As Ai chases Israel off, what are the men in the ambush supposed to do?

answers.text: Rise up and seize the city

cards.question: Once the ambush has taken Ai, Joshua's orders are to ___ the city.

cards.text: Then Joshua wraps it up: "Do as the LORD has commanded! See, I have given you orders." I think that's a man who's DONE taking questions.
So the ambush goes and lies in wait between Bethel and Ai, to the west of Ai. And Joshua spends that night among the people.

cards.question: The next morning, Joshua sleeps in and lets the elders lead the march to Ai.

cards.text: Joshua and the elders of Israel march out in front of the troops, up to Ai. That's a boss who walks in first, not one who sends a memo from home.
The army camps north of Ai, with the valley between them and the city. About five thousand men lie in ambush to the west, between Bethel and Ai.

cards.question: That night, Joshua goes into the valley between his camp and Ai.

cards.text: When the king of Ai sees the Israelites, he hurries out early in the morning with the men of the city to fight, at a spot overlooking the Arabah. But he has no idea an ambush is waiting behind his city.

cards.question: Joshua and all Israel face the army of Ai. What do they do?

answers.text: Let themselves be beaten back and flee
Hold their ground in the valley

cards.text: They flee toward the wilderness, and friend, this time the running is award-winning ACTING. Ai takes the bait and follows Joshua, and they get drawn away from the city.

cards.question: Ai leaves a few guards behind to watch the city while the rest chase Israel.

cards.text: Not a man is left in Ai or Bethel, and the city is wide open. That's leaving the bakery door open with a fresh batch on the counter and a back-in-five sign taped to the glass.

cards.question: The LORD tells Joshua to hold something out toward Ai. What is it?

cards.text: Joshua holds out his battle lance toward Ai. And as soon as he does, the men in ambush rise quickly from their position.

cards.question: The ambush rushes into Ai and captures it. What do they do right away?

cards.text: Picture the men of Ai chasing Israel, and I bet they're feeling GREAT. Then they turn and look back.

cards.question: Behind them, the ___ of their city is rising into the sky.
With their city burning, the men of Ai can still escape in one direction.

cards.text: The Israelites who fled to the wilderness turn on their pursuers, and the chased just became the chasers. Joshua and all Israel see the smoke, turn around and strike down the men of Ai.

cards.question: Then the ambush comes out of the city against them. Where does that leave the men of Ai?

answers.text: Trapped between Israel on both sides
Scattered toward the hills of Bethel

cards.text: Israel strikes them down until no survivor or fugitive remains. But one man is taken alive and brought to Joshua.

cards.question: Who is brought to Joshua alive?

cards.text: Israel returns to Ai and puts it to the sword. Twelve thousand men and women fall that day, all the people of Ai.
Joshua doesn't draw back the hand holding his battle lance until all who lived in Ai are devoted to destruction.

cards.question: This time Israel takes only the cattle and plunder of Ai for themselves, just as the LORD commanded Joshua.

cards.text: So Joshua burns Ai and makes it a permanent heap of ruins, a desolation to this day. He hangs the king of Ai on a tree until evening.

cards.question: At sunset, the body of the king of Ai is taken down and thrown down at the entrance of the city gate. What do they raise over it?

findings.problem: This non-opening story card is five sentences long: the quoted sentence followed by four more sentences. It exceeds the two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The distractor "Stand and fight them" is not false throughout the passage: Joshua and all Israel later turn around and strike down the men of Ai (Joshua 8:21). Use a distractor that never happens in Joshua 8:1-29.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: "Behind them" and "their city" have no antecedent in the question; they rely on the preceding story card to identify the men of Ai. Name the men of Ai in the question itself.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
